correctness.rationale: In odd characteristic the ordinary commutator equals twice the wedge of the odd portions. On the u_1 nonzero stratum, independent fiber dimensions give 24 for five generators and 48 for six; u_1=0,v_1 nonzero points are degenerations. For n<=5 the skew 5-by-5 kernel (and smaller-degree cases) gives a linear degeneration from the remaining locus, proving irreducibility. For n=6 the remaining locus is the rank-40 irreducible quadratic hypersurface in two 20-dimensional three-form spaces, with 12 freely varying five-form coordinates, hence dimension 51; adjoining the 64 even coordinates gives exactly two components of dimensions 112 and 115. Exact independent fiber counts produce the six-generator odd finite-field formula. Verified by literal exterior-product matrix-rank and field-count consistency checks in the standalone script.

value.rationale: This gives a sharp transition from irreducible commuting-pair varieties through five generators to a provably reducible, non-equidimensional variety at six generators; the complete component classification has explicit rational pieces and closed dimensions 112 and 115, together with a field-uniform exact count. Such a structural boundary supplies information distinct from maximal commutative subalgebra dimensions or rank distributions and is motivated by the first appearance of a nondegenerate middle-degree wedge pairing.
